markdown_report:
At 10% research progress, prioritize **recency-weighted, regularized BPR-max** within the corrected GRU4Rec. Its proposed benefits remain unmeasured.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has 22.31% small sampled margins and 9.01% negative-over-positive rankings. These support testing stronger discrimination, without establishing validation failure causes. (2) Users report stale interests displacing current preferences. Recency weighting can emphasize learning from recent transitions, although it cannot identify current intent directly. (3) Users distinguish specific matches from broad affinity. Competitive negatives can challenge broad matches, but unobserved items are not confirmed dislikes.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [GRU4Rec](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) introduces BPR-max to emphasize competitive negatives. Its negative-score regularization offers a direct, small change to this backbone. (2) The [sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) reports dataset-dependent sampling outcomes. Uniform sampling is therefore a useful controlled starting point, not a claimed optimum. (3) [MTAM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) models temporal retention within recurrent recommendation. It motivates a later timestamp-aware extension, but does not prove that positional weighting resolves preference drift.

**Framework.** Organize experiments along three axes: discrimination (pairwise versus BPR-max), supervision allocation (uniform versus recent positions), and retention (ordinary versus time-gated GRU). The immediate gap is a controlled separation of loss and weighting effects.

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| A: recency-weighted BPR-max | 3/7/7/8/3 | O: useful combination, established components; P: reusable objective, limited novelty; U: targets stale and broad matches, cannot verify purpose; M: targets weak margins, training gains may not generalize; D: localized change, masking requires care. |
| B: gap-conditioned GRU retention | 5/7/8/6/6 | O: content-conditioned forgetting, temporal precedents; P: models drift, sparse gaps may mislead; U: targets stale and context-mismatched choices, gaps do not reveal intent; M: may improve separation, indirect mechanism; D: compact gate, predictor timestamp contract uncertain. |
| C: jointly trained title encoder | 4/7/7/6/7 | O: combines semantic and recurrent learning, established ingredients; P: finer matching, sparse text supervision; U: may improve specificity and compatibility cues, descriptions can omit requirements; M: richer features, alignment may worsen; D: one checkpoint, vocabulary integration adds work. |

**Selected algorithm A.** Normalize exponential positional weights within each sequence; apply BPR-max over 16 uniformly sampled negatives excluding training-history positives. Start with temperature 1, recency half-life 10 valid positions, and negative-score penalty 0.01. These are proposed settings, not established optima. It explicitly targets stale-interest dominance and broadly related competitors, plus Electronics’ weak sampled margins.

Compare loss-only, weighting-only, and combined trials against the supplied baseline. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Preserve all four routes, seeds, limits, diagnostics, final-nonpadding readout, and exactly one matching model/checkpoint per category.

idea.description: Recency-weighted regularized BPR-max for the supplied corrected GRU4Rec, with one independently trained model per category. Use a modest uniform negative pool and controlled loss-versus-weighting comparisons.
idea.motivation: Address two observed user-facing failures: older interests displacing recent preferences, and broadly related candidates competing with specific matches. Address the measured weak sampled separation in Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific. These mechanisms are hypotheses; neither improved margins nor recency weighting establishes improved user intent alignment or validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep the supplied GRU architecture and inference scores unchanged, so existing checkpoint and predictor definitions remain compatible. Replace only the training objective and negative sampling. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preserve supplied splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, four-category routing, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Exclude padding, each target, and known training-history positives from negative pools; never inspect held-out positives for exclusions. Sample 16 uniform negatives per valid transition, reducing the pool if necessary. Normalize positional weights per sequence and average over sequences with valid transitions. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Evaluate diagnostic margins using the same sampling protocol across comparisons. No timestamp features or inference changes are required. Final sequence readout must use the final nonpadding index. The baseline source was not supplied, so the following is an integration-ready loss function rather than a replacement train.py.
idea.pseudocode:
import math
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def recency_bpr_max(pos_logits, neg_logits, valid,
                    half_life=10.0, temperature=1.0, score_reg=0.01):
    """pos: [B,L], neg: [B,L,K], valid: [B,L].
    Negatives must already exclude padding and known training positives.
    Compute logits only for valid transitions to avoid padded-state effects.
    """
    valid = valid.bool()
    rows, cols = valid.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    if rows.numel() == 0:
        return pos_logits.sum() * 0.0
    if neg_logits.shape[-1] == 0:
        raise ValueError('At least one eligible negative is required')
    if half_life <= 0 or temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError('half_life and temperature must be positive')

    p = pos_logits[rows, cols].float()
    n = neg_logits[rows, cols].float()
    log_q = F.log_softmax(n / temperature, dim=-1)
    ranking = -torch.logsumexp(
        log_q + F.logsigmoid(p[:, None] - n), dim=-1)
    penalty = score_reg * (log_q.exp() * n.square()).sum(-1)

    # Relative age among valid transitions; works with left padding.
    rank = valid.long().cumsum(dim=1)
    count = valid.sum(dim=1)
    age = count[rows] - rank[rows, cols]
    weight = torch.exp(-math.log(2.0) * age.float() / half_life)
    denom = torch.zeros(pos_logits.shape[0], device=p.device)
    denom.scatter_add_(0, rows, weight)
    per_sequence = torch.zeros_like(denom)
    per_sequence.scatter_add_(
        0, rows, weight * (ranking + penalty) / denom[rows])
    return per_sequence[count > 0].mean()

# Controlled trials, each initializing fresh category models:
# 1. Supplied baseline.
# 2. BPR-max with uniform positional weights.
# 3. Supplied baseline loss with recency weights.
# 4. BPR-max with recency weights.
# Keep sampling identical where applicable to isolate effects.
# Host validation selects one trial by macro HR@10; never fuse checkpoints.

originality.positive: Combines a diagnosis-motivated allocation of supervision with a well-established competitive ranking loss in a controlled GRU experiment.
originality.negative: Both BPR-max and recency weighting are established techniques; this is an empirical hypothesis rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: A small objective change provides a clear foundation for subsequent studies of temporal retention and sampling.
future_potential.negative: No supplied experiment demonstrates improved validation HR@10, immediate-choice endorsements, or functional specificity.

code_difficulty.positive: The loss can be integrated without changing the recurrent backbone or inference architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Negative exclusions, valid-position normalization, and controlled diagnostic sampling require careful integration with the unavailable baseline source.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces competitive ranking objectives including BPR-max and negative-score regularization for recurrent recommendation.
limitations: Does not establish gains for the supplied Amazon splits or the proposed positional weighting.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation negative-sampling study supplied in the search results
contributions: Compares sampling strategies and reports variation across datasets and item popularity.
limitations: Provides no universal guarantee that more competitive negatives improve ranking.

related_work.title: MTAM
contributions: Uses temporal gating and recurrent modeling to capture changing sequential preferences.
limitations: Temporal retention differs from positional loss weighting and requires additional architecture and timestamp integration.
